profiles.name: Corey Cardale Gee
profiles.description: On May 31, 2020 Corey Cardale Gee, 28, of Tampa, FL was arrested for unlawful violation of emergency measures and burglary of an unoccupied structure during protests for George Floyd. He was seen breaking into a Marathon gas station. Sentenced to 8 months in Florida state prison.
profiles.finding: Only third-party arrest listing found; no original-source verified portrait.

profiles.name: Raul Guzman
profiles.description: Raul Guzman, 24, of Lakeland, FL was charged with inciting a riot following his participation in a Black Lives Matter protest at Munn Park on May 31, 2020. According to a witness, Guzman encouraged people to go into the streets and that he wanted to "riot" and "storm" the police department. Sentenced to 1.5 months in Florida state prison plus 18 months probation.
profiles.finding: Sports, racing and Chilean artist namesakes rejected. FOX13 Lakeland case has named booking image; direct fetch failed, pending.

profiles.name: Chelsie Leann Eggers
profiles.description: Chelsie Eggers, 27, of Fargo, ND was charged with arming rioters, attempting to commit assault, rioting, and disobedience of public safety orders after she was arrested in connection with a protest related to the murder of George Floyd on May 30, 2020. Sentenced to 1 month in North Dakota state prison plus 1 year probation.
profiles.finding: Exact and shortened name Fargo searches found no verified portrait; family obituary not sufficient.

profiles.name: Keith Leroy Moreno
profiles.description: Keith Leroy Moreno was arrested on July 1, 2020, after federal investigators accused him of breaking three windows at the Bruce R. Thompson Federal Courthouse in Reno during the May 30 George Floyd demonstrations. He later pleaded guilty to damaging federal property and received a probationary sentence in September 2021. No jail or prison term was imposed in this protest case.
profiles.finding: Nevada court decision and federal list match name; no verified portrait.

profiles.name: Orlando Shalrocko King
profiles.description: Orlando King, 31, of North Charleston, SC was indicted on charges of violating the Anti-Riot Act on May 30, 2020 and felon in possession of a firearm (from an unrelated April 25, 2020 incident). King livestreamed the looting and destruction of a store, the College Market, on Facebook. Sentenced to 24 months federal prison plus 3 years supervised release.
profiles.finding: SC solicitor civil unrest review and sentencing report match; no accepted portrait.

profiles.name: Errick Steven Toa
profiles.description: Errick Steven Toa, 33, jumped on top of an occupied police car and broke its windshield during the May 30, 2020 Fargo ND BLM protest. Charged July 15, 2020. Pleaded guilty; ~10.6 months time served + 2 years supervised release + $390 restitution.
profiles.finding: VNL matching case image inspected: 800x450 two-view booking composite. Deferred for cleaner single portrait. Cass County credit; KFGO alternate failed fetch.

profiles.name: Davon De-Andre Turner
profiles.description: Davon De-Andre Turner was federally prosecuted for carrying an incendiary device into the Minneapolis Police Department’s Third Precinct during the May 28, 2020 protests following George Floyd’s murder. He pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit arson on January 22, 2021. On May 13, 2021, a federal judge sentenced Turner to 36 months in prison, two years of supervised release, and $12 million in joint restitution.
profiles.finding: CBS Minnesota sentencing report matches; no accepted portrait; meme claims not evidence.

profiles.name: Hampton Milton McCoy III
profiles.description: Hampton Milton McCoy III, 29, of Tampa, FL was charged following his involvement in a Black Lives Matter protest over Memorial Day weekend 2020 — initially with burglary of an unoccupied structure and grand theft after allegedly breaking into a Gold and Diamond Source store. He pled no contest to burglary in exchange for the grand theft charge being dropped. Sentenced to 180 days in Florida state prison plus 24 months probation and 50 hours community service.
profiles.finding: Patch Tampa arrests matches; third-party2018 photo needs original-source confirmation, not accepted.

profiles.name: Isaiah JK Lindsey-Salinas
profiles.description: Isaiah Lindsey-Salinas, 23, of Eugene, OR was indicted on charges of rioting, burglary, and theft after being arrested in connection with a May 2020 George Floyd protest in Eugene that turned violent — people damaging property, robbing businesses, and setting a fire in the middle of an intersection. Felony charges dropped; found guilty of misdemeanors. Sentenced to about 5 days in Oregon state prison.
profiles.finding: Eugene exact/shortened queries no usable portrait; people-search result not identity proof.

profiles.name: Marcus Marlvin Hunt
profiles.description: In May 2020 in St. Louis, MO, Marcus Marlvin Hunt, 29, was charged with distribution of information relating to explosives after providing a recipe for napalm on Facebook. He said in a Facebook live video, "I am trying to give y'all good information on weapons, armaments that you might need later on." The St. Louis Joint Terrorism Task Force treated this as evidence of imminent acts of violence. Case dropped.
profiles.finding: Prosecution Project case match; school alumni listing not sufficient portrait evidence.

profiles.name: Michael J. Avery
profiles.description: On May 25-29, 2020 Michael J. Avery, 28, was charged with rioting after posting calls to action on Facebook under "Mike Avery" regarding Black Lives Matter protests in Minnesota. Posts included "CALLING OUT ALL THE SHOOTERS, ALL THE PEOPLE WHO DON'T GIVE AF" and "level RED ACTION." On May 30 he traveled to St. Louis to continue protesting, posting about how looting occurred in Minneapolis and encouraging "the masses" to participate. Case dropped.
profiles.finding: Deceased people, physician, author and police-accountability attorney namesakes not established defendant, excluded.

profiles.name: Nathan Joseph Waller
profiles.description: Nathan Joseph Waller, 25, of Erie, PA was sentenced to 9 to 21.5 months in state prison and 60 days on electronic monitoring after pleading guilty to three criminal charges following a series of Black Lives Matter protests in May 2020. He was accused of throwing objects at police officers on a roof at Erie City Hall as they tried to disperse a large crowd outside of the city police station and of carrying the top of a broken parking meter into an apartment building.
profiles.finding: Dover UK offender, cricketer and historical soldier excluded. Erie LinkedIn same name/location lacks case link.

profiles.name: Galen Sol Shireman-Grabowski
profiles.description: Galen Sol Shireman-Grabowski, age 24, locked himself to a helicopter used by Mountain Valley Pipeline crews in Ellison, Virginia in October 2019, damaging the helicopter. Charged with multiple felonies and misdemeanors; pleaded guilty to four counts and received a 12-month suspended sentence plus $14,030.41 in restitution.
profiles.finding: Exact/shortened query no usable portrait; obituary similar names not proof.

profiles.name: Timothy Hummel
profiles.description: Timothy Hummel, 26, of Denver, sent threatening messages in 2019 to a U.S. Customs and Immigration Enforcement office threatening ICE agents and their families. Pleaded guilty August 10, 2020 to threatening to murder federal law enforcement officers; 3 years supervised release, no prison.
profiles.finding: Lawyer, baseball player and1961-born obituary unrelated to26-year-old Denver defendant.

profiles.name: Henry Trigos-Celon
profiles.description: Henry Trigos-Celon, age 43, ELN member; detained in September 2020. Pleaded guilty in U.S. federal court to the ELN cocaine-trafficking conspiracy.
profiles.finding: AP Fernando Vergara extradition portrait via Houston Chronicle and Reuters-style Infobae caption promising; image/rights review pending.

profiles.name: Renea Goddard
profiles.description: Renea Goddard is one of the four Little Rock, Arkansas defendants — alongside Mujera Benjamin Lunga’ho, Cody Nowlin, and Angel Espinosa-Villegas — federally prosecuted for the torching of Little Rock police vehicles during the protests that followed the police murder of George Floyd. In September 2022 she pleaded guilty to conspiracy to possess a Molotov cocktail and was sentenced to 18 months in federal prison. She began her sentence in 2024.
profiles.finding: Them author portrait and academic page leads require independent link to Little Rock case; childhood Osan image not accepted.

profiles.name: Esmond Adams
profiles.description: Record under review: this entry appears to misidentify Judge Kimberly Esmond Adams, who presided over the Stop Cop City prosecution, as a defendant. No corresponding prisoner identity has been verified.
profiles.finding: Existing record flags judge misidentification; official Fulton court judge page supports concern. No prisoner identity verified; do not attach judge portrait.

profiles.name: Annarella Rivera
profiles.description:
Annarella Rivera is publicly documented through a federal prosecution involving attacks on pregnancy resource centers that counsel abortion alternatives. The government characterized the conduct as ideologically driven intimidation—vandalism and threatening messages directed at staff and facilities in the context of polarized activism around reproductive rights—rather than conventional protest activity.
In March 2023, the U.S. Department of Justice announced a superseding indictment alleging Rivera participated in a conspiracy connected to targeted attacks on facilities in Florida and describing related allegations under the FACE Act. DOJ later reported that Rivera pleaded guilty (June 14, 2024) to a civil-rights conspiracy, and that she was sentenced (Sept. 12, 2024) to 30 days in prison and 60 days of home detention.
profiles.finding: ABCF publishes subject's first-person statement with recognizable portrait and matching Florida codefendants/case.550x1024 inspected; original retained. Photographer/license unstated.

profiles.name: Kamile Dincsoy
profiles.description: Kamile Dincsoy was charged in Riverside County, California, with felony vandalism over red paint placed on the Historic Riverside County Courthouse during an abortion-rights demonstration on July 9, 2022. Prosecutors filed the charge on September 30 and obtained an arrest warrant on October 4 after learning that she lived outside the county. She did not appear at the defendants’ October 6 arraignment. The available public record establishes a warrant, not an arrest or confinement.
profiles.finding: MyNewsLA case match shows stock courtroom, rejected. Turkish feminist/translator namesake not independently matched.

profiles.name: Brandon Michael Althof Long
profiles.description: In Cleveland, OH, Brandon Michael Althof Long, 23, and Devon Bryce Poland, 22, were both charged with conspiracy to riot, conspiracy to use fire to commit a felony, interstate travel to riot, and transporting a firearm in furtherance of civil disorder following arrest after a curfew. Texts showed they made arrangements to travel from PA to participate in Cleveland riots; weapons in their vehicle included a hammer, fire-starter containers, a glass liquor bottle, and a Glock semi-automatic with ammunition. Case dismissed March 2021.
profiles.finding: Federal Ohio suppression decision matches; no verified portrait.
